newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN RULING SOCIALISTS DISCUSS PM NOMINATION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN RULING SOCIALISTS DISCUSS PM NOMINATION.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party (BSP) on Wednesday began discussing with its parliamentary allies the nomination of powerfull Interiour Minister Nikolai Dobrev to replace Zhan Videnov who resigned last month.
BSP chairman Georgi Parvanov told reporters the party would seek a broad support for the future prime minister, who has yet to be approved by parliament.

If approved, Dobrev, will then hand his mandate to form a new cabinet to outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev, meet President -Elect Petar Stoyanov, who is due to take office on January 19, and meet the Sofia ambassadors of the European Union member-states, said Parvanov.

Political analysts said that Dobrev's nomination may be opposed by some Socialist deputies, which fear that his access to information may endanger their careers and propose a weaker figure for prime minister like the speaker of parliament, Blagovest Sendov, who is a mathematician.
Bulgarian police files from the communist era have never been made public as they were in East Germany.
Analaysts said that Dobrev was likely to pass the vote by a narrow margin.
Videnov resigned at a BSP congress in December after months of criticism of his handling of the economy, sparking a showdown between party hardliners and reformists.
The meeting, held behind closed doors, is expected to end later on Wednesday.
